subject: Bringing categorical exogenous variables into model

messages.author: 52d6369876320d8b
messages.subject: Bringing categorical exogenous variables into model
parts:
I'm having trouble understanding the behavior of conditional.x when treating some exogenous variables as categorical.

Here's a simplified model demonstrating my confusion. I have two exogenous variables, gender (binary) and political orientation (Likert-scale/categorical). I also have a latent construct, risk aversion (measured by four Likert-scale/categorical observations), and an outcome variable (Likert-scale/categorical).

I'd like to assess whether the risk aversion construct explains some of the effect of gender and political orientation on the outcome. To do this, I'd like to compare two models: in the first (M1), the structural model is "outcome ~ gender + pol_orient"; in the second (M2), the structural model is "outcome ~ gender + pol_orient + risk_av".

I expected that the regression coefficients for outcome~gender and outcome~pol_orient would be different between M1 and M2. This is indeed the case when I treat all variables as continuous. However, when I specify that the categorical variables are ordered (by specifying "ordered=T" and pulling pol_orient into the latent space with "lat_pol_orient =~ 1*pol_orient" and "pol_orient ~~ 0*pol_orient"), the regression coefficient for outcome~gender is the same in both M1 and M2:

M1 <- 'risk_av =~ RAV1 + RAV2 + RAV3 + RAV4
            lat_pol_orient =~ 1*pol_orient
            pol_orient ~~ 0*pol_orient
            outcome ~ gender + lat_pol_orient'
M2 <- 'risk_av =~ RAV1 + RAV2 + RAV3 + RAV4
            lat_pol_orient =~ 1*pol_orient
            pol_orient ~~ 0*pol_orient
            outcome ~ gender + lat_pol_orient + risk_av'
M1.fit <- sem(M1.model, data, std.lv=T, ordered=T, conditional.x=F)
M2.fit <- sem(M2.model, data, std.lv=T, ordered=T, conditional.x=F)
# expected different estimates for outcome~gender in M1.fit and M2.fit, but they're the same

Questions:

1) Is my method for treating the exogenous 'political orientation ' variable as categorical ("lat_pol_orient =~ 1*pol_orient" and "pol_orient ~~ 0*pol_orient" with ordered=T) correct?

2) My understanding is that I should set conditional.x=F because I don't want to "condition out" exogenous variables like gender in my model. Is this correct?

3) When I treat everything as continuous (by setting ordered=F) the estimates of outcome~gender are different in M1.fit and M2.fit as I expected. Why does modeling some variables as categorical make a difference here? Is there something relevant about the DWLS procedure that I don't understand?

Thanks very much!
Matt

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Bringing categorical exogenous variables into model
parts:
when I specify that the categorical variables are ordered (by specifying "ordered=T"), the regression coefficient for outcome~gender is the same

Because gender is exogenous.

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

You are tricking lavaan into treating pol_orient as endogneous by making it a single-indicator factor, but that would imply you need to fix its "latent" scale AND its factor loading to 1, because it's latent response does not have an implicit scale.  You are using the default delta method, so residual variances are not a model parameter that you can fix to zero:

            pol_orient ~~ 0*pol_orient

To do this, set parameterization = "theta" and fix the loading and "factor" variance to 1.
1) Is my method for treating the exogenous 'political orientation ' variable as categorical ("lat_pol_orient =~ 1*pol_orient" and "pol_orient ~~ 0*pol_orient" with ordered=T) correct?

There is no "correct".  You can treat it as continuous without assuming it is normal because it is exogenous (if you don't treat it like a single-indicator factor).  Then its effect will be in reference to its observed ordinal scale (e.g., 1-5 Likert?).  If you model its latent response, then you can only really interpret its standardized slope (i.e., in units of SD).
2) My understanding is that I should set conditional.x=F because I don't want to "condition out" exogenous variables like gender in my model. Is this correct?

It is arbitrary, but conditioning them out can make estimation less of a burden because your model parameters only need to reproduce the residual polychoric correlation matrix among endogenous latent responses.  Conditioning on exogenous variables is what your model is already doing (i.e., regressing on gender and political orientation), so I don't see why you would not want to do that.
